summary: While frontier vision-language models demonstrate strong capabilities in user interface (UI) navigation, their high inference costs prohibit everyday use. Conversely, smaller models trained via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or offline reinforcement learning often memorize static trajectories, leading to brittle execution and an inability to recover from errors.
takeaways: Conversely, smaller models trained via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or offline reinforcement learning often memorize static trajectories, leading to brittle execution and an inability to recover from errors.
To address these limitations, we propose a novel online reinforcement learning framework that trains UI navigation agents directly on live iOS applications.
Our framework decouples the agent into two specialized components: a Planning agent and a UI Grounding model.
